title: Distill the LLM, Don't Serve It: Search & Personalization at DoorDash — Raghav Saboo, DoorDash
talk_summary: DoorDash uses expensive LLM reasoning offline to produce graded relevance labels, semantic IDs, and structured user memory, then distills those into cheap small models and shared representations that serve retrieval, ranking, and content generation at scale. The core lesson is 'distill, don't serve': capture LLM reasoning once offline as reusable artifacts rather than making online LLM calls the product architecture.

takeaways.technique: Offline distillation of expensive reasoning into cheap labelers
takeaways.what_they_do: Use a strong LLM once offline to generate high-precision graded labels from a small human seed set, then fine-tune a lightweight model (e.g. GPT-4o-mini) to label the full catalog cheaply and quickly.

takeaways.technique: Human-seeded golden set with LLM audit of suspicious labels
takeaways.what_they_do: Build a small high-quality human-labeled seed set, then audit disagreements (e.g. human says irrelevant but item converts well) by sending them to a stronger LLM with more granular prompts, and reconcile against taxonomy models to raise precision.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if a human label says you know that an item is irrelevant but that item performs very well on add to cart or conversions, we send that case to a stronger LLM

takeaways.what_they_do: Represent each user as structured memory blocks (durable prefs, real-time session state, stated prefs) materialized as text, embeddings, and graph/tree forms, decoupled from downstream consumers.
takeaways.evidence_quote: each consumer's memory is multi materialized in multiple forms

takeaways.technique: Learned semantic IDs as shared compact representation
takeaways.what_they_do: Assign each item a short hierarchical learned code where prefixes capture broad neighborhoods and later tokens capture fine distinctions, usable by all downstream models and enabling cross-category links and cold-start.
takeaways.evidence_quote: each item gets this hierarchical code and the prefix captures broad neighborhoods

takeaways.technique: Shared representations power many downstream use cases
takeaways.what_they_do: Once labels, semantic IDs, and memory exist as shared primitives, the same artifacts feed retrieval, ranking, and generation rather than each surface rebuilding its own signal.
takeaways.evidence_quote: once you have these primitives, they can power, you know, retrieval, ranking, content generation, etc.

takeaways.technique: Batch/offline generation with existing serving stack for hydration
takeaways.what_they_do: Generate collections offline via LLM batch jobs, then use existing retrieval/ranking for item hydration and ranking at serving time rather than calling the LLM online.
takeaways.evidence_quote: because this is all batch and uh generated offline through LLMs, we are able to still use our uh existing retrieval and ranking stack
takeaways.numbers: ~1% order rate, 6% active users in pets vertical
